note: v1 97.72 (seeds 0/11 97.72/97.49), first draft of ROLLING / BROKEN TECHNO built on an auditory-streaming illusion, THE GALLOP SPLITS (van Noorden). Two short bleeps play A-B-A-rest every beat: while B sits a semitone or two from A you hear one galloping stream; pull B away (a fifth, an octave, a tenth) and the gallop vanishes into two separate streams, A twice as fast as B, though no note's timing changes. The break pulls them apart; the peak swings the gap every four bars (2, 16, 3, 19, 2, 12, 4, 24 semitones), so the ear flips between one gallop and two streams, and B pans right as it splits. Under it: a broken 909 kick (1, and-of-2, 3-and, a ghost), a rolling reese in sixteenths with octave jumps, pumping. 130 bpm, 4:28.

v2 88.28 (seeds 0/11 88.28/88.08 vs v1 re-scored with Harry's 7.0 88.19/88.03): polish by taking away. The gallop - the illusion everything hangs on - ran almost non-stop for four minutes, a hard bright bleep; now it breathes and is rounder. The square under the sine is quieter, a 3.2 kHz low-pass takes off its edge and more of it goes into the space delay; it enters only after eight bars of A have set up the bass, rests for the last eight bars of B so the break's split arrives after a gap, and drops out for two bars in every eight of the peak - so each time it returns, close or split, you hear it fresh.

v3 90.92 (seeds 0/11 90.92/90.95, level with v2 re-scored 91.17/90.94): THE BREATHING REESE, Harry's 'better LFO use'. The rolling reese sat still for four minutes; now a slow sine LFO, one cycle every eight bars, sweeps a resonant low-pass over it (about 1 to 4 kHz), so the bass's sixteenths open and close like a tide under the gallop and each eight-bar phrase has a shape. Measured 15-19 dB under the mix as a difference - a movement, not a new part. (A deeper sweep, 300 Hz to 2.5 kHz, hollowed the low mids too far, spectrum 96 -> 82; chirper-two's new machine-kit in place of the 909 needs its own mix first, 85.)

v4 90.83 (seeds 0/11 90.83/90.87, level with v3 re-scored 90.84/90.87): THE HELD BREATH, a pacing polish for the drop. The break pulls the gallop apart until it is two separate streams; its very last beat is now cut to silence, and the peak's first hard kick lands out of the gap, so the return of the broken groove (and the gallop snapping back to one stream) hits as a drop instead of just continuing. (Tried chirper-two's rumble kick here as on Where Is the One: 89.8, the broken kick's sections blur, so the 909 stays.)

v5 90.78 (seeds 0/11 90.78/90.87, level with v4 re-scored 90.96/90.99): THE TIDE TURNS - songwriting, not a new layer. For four minutes the whole track sat on one A; now, in the second groove and the peak, the floor moves under the illusion: the rolling reese's root and the gallop's A note step together A, F, C, G, eight bars each (the gap between the gallop's two notes kept, so the split still works on every chord), then home. The first groove and the break stay on A, so the harmony arrives as the second half's reward, and the peak's swings between one gallop and two streams now happen over a changing floor - deep and moving rather than a static loop.
